title: The mirror in the Arnolfini Portrait
hook: A tiny mirror in a 1434 painting shows two people who are not in the room.
peek: At the back of Jan van Eyck's Arnolfini Portrait hangs a small round mirror. Look closely and it reflects the couple from behind, plus two more figures standing in the doorway. Above it, van Eyck wrote that he was there.
lede: Jan van Eyck's Arnolfini Portrait of 1434, now in the National Gallery in London, shows a richly dressed couple in a room in Bruges. On the back wall hangs a small convex mirror. It reflects the whole room in miniature, including the couple seen from behind and two extra figures standing in the doorway, where the viewer would be.

bullets.text: Above the mirror, in fancy script on the wall, van Eyck wrote 'Johannes de eyck fuit hic 1434': Jan van Eyck was here. Painters usually signed with 'made this', so the wording reads almost like a witness's note or a bit of graffiti.
One of the two tiny people in the reflection may be van Eyck himself, standing just where the painter would have stood. Nobody knows who the other is.
The mirror's frame holds ten even smaller painted circles, each showing a scene from the life of Christ. They are so small they are easy to miss, yet each scene is clearly painted.

In 1934 the art historian Erwin Panofsky argued the painting records a wedding, with the two reflected men as witnesses and the picture as a kind of certificate. Many historians now doubt this, and even who the couple were is debated.
